nodes.summary: The covering recurrence is `⊥` exactly when no selection reaches the target.
nodes.title: Covering recurrence is bottom iff no selection reaches the target

nodes.summary: The covering recurrence: the best total value of a selection with total weight at least `L`, `⊥` if none exists. The residual target `L - weight` is truncated subtraction.
nodes.title: Covering recurrence for multiple-choice knapsack

nodes.summary: The packing recurrence is `⊥` exactly when no selection fits the capacity.
nodes.title: Packing recurrence is bottom iff no selection fits the capacity

nodes.summary: The packing recurrence: the best total value of a selection with total weight at most `c`, `⊥` if none exists.
nodes.title: Packing recurrence for multiple-choice knapsack

nodes.summary: The covering recurrence is attained: a finite value is the value of a selection of total weight at least `L`.
nodes.title: Covering recurrence is attained by a covering selection

nodes.summary: The packing recurrence is attained: a finite value is the value of a feasible selection.
nodes.title: Packing recurrence is attained by a feasible selection

nodes.summary: A selection chooses exactly one item from each group, in group order.

nodes.summary: A knapsack item with a natural weight and a value in `β`.

nodes.summary: The covering recurrence is an upper bound: every selection of total weight at least `L` has value at most `bestCovering`.
nodes.title: Covering recurrence bounds every covering selection's value

nodes.summary: The packing recurrence is an upper bound: every feasible selection's value is at most `bestPacking`.
nodes.title: Packing recurrence bounds every feasible selection's value

nodes.summary: The bottom-up packing table: for each suffix of the groups, the row of best values at capacities `0, …, capacity`, each row computed from the next one by one scan of its group per cell.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
